-- ============================================================
-- S24a: Extend consent_form_templates.kind with photo_release,
--       aftercare, reach_ink. Ships alongside the new default
--       templates seeded in lib/consent/seed-templates.ts.
-- ============================================================
-- The original CREATE TABLE for consent_form_templates lives in an
-- earlier bootstrap not present in this repo's migrations dir, so we
-- don't know the exact constraint name used by Postgres. To guarantee
-- safety + idempotency on re-run we:
--   1. Pattern-match every CHECK on consent_form_templates whose
--      definition references `kind` and DROP it — handles both the
--      name we'd expect and any PG-autogenerated variant.
--   2. Install a single canonical kind check with the 9 allowed values.
--   3. Same pattern for retention_years — we widen the upper bound to
--      20 years in case the original CHECK caps it below 10 (the REACH
--      seed uses 10y per EU Annex XVII retention).
--
-- No data migration needed — existing rows use values inside the new
-- ranges. Migration is safe to run multiple times.

-- ── 1. Drop any CHECK on `kind` regardless of its autogenerated name.
do $$
declare r record;
begin
  for r in
    select conname
    from pg_constraint
    where conrelid = 'public.consent_form_templates'::regclass
      and contype = 'c'
      and pg_get_constraintdef(oid) ilike '%kind%'
  loop
    execute format(
      'alter table public.consent_form_templates drop constraint %I',
      r.conname
    );
  end loop;
end;
$$;

-- ── 2. Install the canonical kind constraint with the 9 allowed values.
alter table public.consent_form_templates
  add constraint consent_form_templates_kind_check
  check (
    kind in (
      'tattoo',
      'piercing',
      'pmu',
      'touch_up',
      'minor',
      'custom',
      'photo_release',
      'aftercare',
      'reach_ink'
    )
  );

comment on constraint consent_form_templates_kind_check
  on public.consent_form_templates is
  'S24a: extended with photo_release, aftercare, reach_ink for the Forms Page rebuild. Drives icon + label lookup in TemplateCard and the filter dropdown in TemplatesGrid.';

-- ── 3. Ensure retention_years allows 1..20 (REACH seed needs 10y).
-- Same pattern-match DROP so we don't care about the original name.
do $$
declare r record;
begin
  for r in
    select conname
    from pg_constraint
    where conrelid = 'public.consent_form_templates'::regclass
      and contype = 'c'
      and pg_get_constraintdef(oid) ilike '%retention_years%'
  loop
    execute format(
      'alter table public.consent_form_templates drop constraint %I',
      r.conname
    );
  end loop;
end;
$$;

alter table public.consent_form_templates
  add constraint consent_form_templates_retention_years_check
  check (retention_years between 1 and 20);

comment on constraint consent_form_templates_retention_years_check
  on public.consent_form_templates is
  'S24a: widened to 1..20 years so REACH default (10y per EU Annex XVII) can seed without violating a pre-existing narrower check.';

-- ============================================================
-- S24b: consent_auto_send_rules — the rule-engine table for the
-- Forms Page rebuild. Each row binds a booking-lifecycle trigger
-- to a template + timing + channel set. The worker reads this table
-- in F3c to decide what to send when; this migration (F3a) ships
-- only the schema + seed function so the UI (F3b) can read/write.
-- ============================================================

-- Sage M1 fix — idempotent re-run. Drop existing trigger + policies ONLY if
-- the table is already present. A fresh install goes straight to CREATE TABLE
-- below; a re-run tears down the policies/trigger so the CREATE statements at
-- the bottom don't collide.
do $$
begin
  if to_regclass('public.consent_auto_send_rules') is not null then
    execute 'drop trigger if exists consent_auto_send_rules_updated_at on consent_auto_send_rules';
    execute 'drop policy if exists "consent_auto_send_rules_select" on consent_auto_send_rules';
    execute 'drop policy if exists "consent_auto_send_rules_insert" on consent_auto_send_rules';
    execute 'drop policy if exists "consent_auto_send_rules_update" on consent_auto_send_rules';
    execute 'drop policy if exists "consent_auto_send_rules_delete" on consent_auto_send_rules';
  end if;
end;
$$;

create table if not exists consent_auto_send_rules (
  id              uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  studio_id       uuid not null references studios(id) on delete cascade,

  -- Which lifecycle event fires this rule. The 5 v1 triggers match the
  -- Forms scoping doc; custom triggers require a schema change (intentional
  -- — gives us a policy-level lever before opening up to user-defined triggers).
  trigger         text not null check (trigger in (
    'any_booking',
    'first_time_client',
    'minor_client',
    'session_complete',
    'eu_region'
  )),

  -- Which template to send. FK cascades — if a studio archives the template
  -- this rule dies with it, by design (no orphaned rules pointing nowhere).
  template_id     uuid not null references consent_form_templates(id) on delete cascade,

  -- When to send relative to the trigger event.
  timing          text not null default 'immediately' check (timing in (
    'immediately',              -- fire the moment the trigger fires
    'hours_before_session',     -- timing_value = hours; only valid for booking triggers
    'minutes_after_complete'    -- timing_value = minutes; only valid for session_complete
  )),
  timing_value    int not null default 0 check (timing_value >= 0 and timing_value <= 24 * 30),

  -- Which outbound channels to use. At least one must be selected.
  channels        text[] not null default array['sms', 'email']::text[],

  -- Owner toggle — the worker skips disabled rules. Keeps history intact
  -- instead of deleting rows when studios want to pause a trigger.
  enabled         boolean not null default true,

  -- True for the 5 pre-configured rules seeded on studio creation. Lets the
  -- UI distinguish "InkOS default" from "studio custom" (we style them the
  -- same on the rules list but the badge changes).
  is_default      boolean not null default false,

  created_at      timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at      timestamptz not null default now(),

  -- One rule per trigger per studio. v1 constraint — custom triggers can
  -- coexist with the 5 defaults because each trigger is unique. When we
  -- open up multiple rules per trigger (e.g. different rules per service),
  -- drop this and add a priority column.
  unique (studio_id, trigger),

  -- Channels must be a non-empty subset of {sms, email}.
  constraint consent_auto_send_rules_channels_check
